    I/O -- Parsers & Writers¶

    Functions and classes for reading and writing EnergyPlus models in IDF (text) and epJSON (JSON) formats.

    Convenience Loaders¶

    Top-level convenience functions:

    • load_idf(path, version=None, *, as_type=None, since=None, before=None, strict_parsing=True, strict=True, preserve_formatting=False, normalize_choices=True, encoding=None) for IDF files.
    • load_epjson(path, version=None, *, as_type=None, since=None, before=None, strict_parsing=True, strict=True, preserve_formatting=False, normalize_choices=True) for epJSON files.

    Both parse strictly by default: a malformed object or an unknown object type raises IDFParseError, and strict_parsing=False skips it instead. Both return an AnyIDFDocument unless as_type=, since= or before= names the model's release; see Typed for a Release.

    strict governs field access on the loaded objects: an unknown field name raises InvalidFieldError, or returns None with strict=False, and an assigned value the schema refuses raises ValidationFailedError.

    encoding=None reads an IDF file as UTF-8 when its bytes are valid UTF-8, and as latin-1 otherwise. save_idf() writes the document back in the same encoding.

    load_idf_with_diagnostics() reads tolerantly and returns the document together with the recoverable findings it skipped; it takes the arguments of load_idf() except strict_parsing.

    Load an IDF file and return its document.

    A model's EnergyPlus release is read from its file, so a type checker cannot know it: the document is typed as AnyIDFDocument, which offers what every supported release has. Name the release with as_type=, or a range of releases with since= and before=, to type it for that release; the release is checked once the file is read, as idfkit.versioned.as_version checks it.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    path Path | str

    Path to the IDF file

    		 required
    version tuple[int, int, int] | None

    Optional version override (major, minor, patch): the release whose schema the file is read with. A Version object in the file still sets doc.version, and that is what as_type=, since= and before= are checked against.

    		 None
    as_type DocumentTypeTarget | None

    The document type of the release the file must be, such as IDFDocumentV9_4 from idfkit.versioned, or a tuple of them. The document is returned typed as it, or as the union of the tuple's types. A type argument states the strictness: IDFDocumentV9_4[Literal[False]] loads a non-strict document, as strict=False does.

    		 None
    since ReleaseBound | None

    The first release of a range the file must be in: its document type, "major.minor" or a version tuple. The document is typed as the union of the range's releases.

    		 None
    before ReleaseBound | None

    The release that range stops before, the same way.

    		 None
    strict_parsing bool

    If True, fail fast on malformed IDF objects (default: True)

    		 True
    strict bool

    When True, accessing or setting an unknown field name on any IDFObject raises InvalidFieldError instead of returning None, and assigning a value the schema refuses raises ValidationFailedError, as add() does.

    		 True
    preserve_formatting bool

    When True, build a Concrete Syntax Tree (CST) so that write_idf and save_idf reproduce the original formatting, comments, and whitespace for unmodified objects. Choice normalization does not affect this: an unmodified object is written as read. Without it, save() over this file drops its ! comments and re-sorts its objects, and warns with FormattingLossWarning when the file has comments.

    		 False
    normalize_choices bool

    When True (the default), each choice value is stored in the spelling its schema declares, whatever case the file used: a surface the file calls WALL has surface_type == "Wall", as its Literal type says, so an exhaustive match holds on models you did not write. EnergyPlus reads choices case-insensitively, so no simulation changes. False keeps the file's text, and a choice field's Literal type then does not hold; see IDFDocument.normalize_choices.

    		 True
    encoding str | None

    The file's text encoding. None (the default) reads it as UTF-8 when its bytes are valid UTF-8 and as latin-1 otherwise, dropping a UTF-8 byte-order mark. save_idf writes the document back in the same encoding.

    		 None

    Returns:

    Type Description
    AnyIDFDocument

    The parsed document: an AnyIDFDocument, or typed as as_type= or the
    AnyIDFDocument

    since=/before= range when one is given.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    TypeError

    If the file's release is not the one as_type= names or is outside the since=/before= range; or, before the file is read, if both as_type= and a range are given, as_type= is not a document type, or its type argument states a strict document while strict=False.
    ValueError

    Before the file is read, if since= or before= names no supported release, or the range holds none.

    Examples:

    Load a DOE reference building and list its zones:

    ```python
model = load_idf("RefBldgSmallOfficeNew2004.idf")
print(f"Loaded {len(model)} objects")
for zone in model["Zone"]:
    print(zone.name)
```

    State the release, so the model is checked against that release's object types:

    ```python
from idfkit.versioned import IDFDocumentV9_4

legacy = load_idf("legacy.idf", as_type=IDFDocumentV9_4)
recent = load_idf("model.idf", since="9.6")  # 9.6, 22.1, ... and the latest
recent["Space"].first()  # Space exists in every one of those releases
```

    Override the version for a legacy model:

    ```python
model = load_idf("pre_v9_building.idf", version=(9, 6, 0))
```

    Lossless round-trip:

    ```python
model = load_idf("building.idf", preserve_formatting=True)
save_idf(model, "building_copy.idf")  # byte-identical
```

    def load_idf(
    path: Path | str,
    version: tuple[int, int, int] | None = None,
    *,
    as_type: DocumentTypeTarget | None = None,
    since: ReleaseBound | None = None,
    before: ReleaseBound | None = None,
    strict_parsing: bool = True,
    strict: bool = True,
    preserve_formatting: bool = False,
    normalize_choices: bool = True,
    encoding: str | None = None,
) -> AnyIDFDocument:
    """
    Load an IDF file and return its document.

    A model's EnergyPlus release is read from its file, so a type checker cannot know it: the
    document is typed as ``AnyIDFDocument``, which offers what every supported release has. Name
    the release with ``as_type=``, or a range of releases with ``since=`` and ``before=``, to type
    it for that release; the release is checked once the file is read, as
    [idfkit.versioned.as_version][idfkit.versioned.as_version] checks it.

    Args:
        path: Path to the IDF file
        version: Optional version override (major, minor, patch): the release whose schema the
            file is read with. A ``Version`` object in the file still sets ``doc.version``, and
            that is what ``as_type=``, ``since=`` and ``before=`` are checked against.
        as_type: The document type of the release the file must be, such as ``IDFDocumentV9_4``
            from [idfkit.versioned][idfkit.versioned], or a tuple of them. The document is returned typed as
            it, or as the union of the tuple's types. A type argument states the strictness:
            ``IDFDocumentV9_4[Literal[False]]`` loads a non-strict document, as ``strict=False`` does.
        since: The first release of a range the file must be in: its document type,
            ``"major.minor"`` or a version tuple. The document is typed as the union of the
            range's releases.
        before: The release that range stops before, the same way.
        strict_parsing: If True, fail fast on malformed IDF objects (default: True)
        strict: When ``True``, accessing or setting an unknown field name on any
            IDFObject raises [InvalidFieldError][idfkit.exceptions.InvalidFieldError] instead
            of returning ``None``, and assigning a value the schema refuses raises
            [ValidationFailedError][idfkit.exceptions.ValidationFailedError], as ``add()`` does.
        preserve_formatting: When ``True``, build a Concrete Syntax Tree
            (CST) so that [write_idf][idfkit.writers.write_idf] and [save_idf][idfkit.writers.save_idf]
            reproduce the original
            formatting, comments, and whitespace for unmodified objects. Choice
            normalization does not affect this: an unmodified object is written as read.
            Without it, ``save()`` over this file drops its ``!`` comments and re-sorts its
            objects, and warns with [FormattingLossWarning][idfkit.exceptions.FormattingLossWarning]
            when the file has comments.
        normalize_choices: When ``True`` (the default), each choice value is stored in the
            spelling its schema declares, whatever case the file used: a surface the file
            calls ``WALL`` has ``surface_type == "Wall"``, as its ``Literal`` type says, so an
            exhaustive ``match`` holds on models you did not write. EnergyPlus reads choices
            case-insensitively, so no simulation changes. ``False`` keeps the file's text, and
            a choice field's ``Literal`` type then does not hold; see
            [IDFDocument.normalize_choices][idfkit.document.IDFDocument.normalize_choices].
        encoding: The file's text encoding. ``None`` (the default) reads it as UTF-8 when its
            bytes are valid UTF-8 and as latin-1 otherwise, dropping a UTF-8 byte-order mark.
            [save_idf][idfkit.writers.save_idf] writes the document back in the same encoding.

    Returns:
        The parsed document: an ``AnyIDFDocument``, or typed as ``as_type=`` or the
        ``since=``/``before=`` range when one is given.

    Raises:
        TypeError: If the file's release is not the one ``as_type=`` names or is outside the
            ``since=``/``before=`` range; or, before the file is read, if both ``as_type=`` and a
            range are given, ``as_type=`` is not a document type, or its type argument states a
            strict document while ``strict=False``.
        ValueError: Before the file is read, if ``since=`` or ``before=`` names no supported
            release, or the range holds none.

    Examples:
        Load a DOE reference building and list its zones:

            ```python
            model = load_idf("RefBldgSmallOfficeNew2004.idf")
            print(f"Loaded {len(model)} objects")
            for zone in model["Zone"]:
                print(zone.name)
            ```

        State the release, so the model is checked against that release's object types:

            ```python
            from idfkit.versioned import IDFDocumentV9_4

            legacy = load_idf("legacy.idf", as_type=IDFDocumentV9_4)
            recent = load_idf("model.idf", since="9.6")  # 9.6, 22.1, ... and the latest
            recent["Space"].first()  # Space exists in every one of those releases
            ```

        Override the version for a legacy model:

            ```python
            model = load_idf("pre_v9_building.idf", version=(9, 6, 0))
            ```

        Lossless round-trip:

            ```python
            model = load_idf("building.idf", preserve_formatting=True)
            save_idf(model, "building_copy.idf")  # byte-identical
            ```
    """
    strict = _prepare(as_type, since, before, strict, version)
    doc = parse_idf(
        Path(path),
        version=version,
        encoding=encoding,
        strict_parsing=strict_parsing,
        strict=strict,
        preserve_formatting=preserve_formatting,
        normalize_choices=normalize_choices,
    )
    return _narrow(doc, path, as_type, since, before)

    Load an epJSON file and return its document.

    The document is typed as AnyIDFDocument unless as_type=, since= or before= names its release, as for load_idf.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    path Path | str

    Path to the epJSON file

    		 required
    version tuple[int, int, int] | None

    Optional version override (major, minor, patch)

    		 None
    as_type DocumentTypeTarget | None

    The document type of the release the file must be, or a tuple of them, as for load_idf.

    		 None
    since ReleaseBound | None

    The first release of a range the file must be in, as for load_idf.

    		 None
    before ReleaseBound | None

    The release that range stops before, as for load_idf.

    		 None
    strict_parsing bool

    When True (the default), an object type the schema does not have raises IDFParseError, as load_idf does, and the message suggests the closest type; EnergyPlus refuses such a file. False skips it with a logged warning.

    		 True
    strict bool

    When True, accessing or setting an unknown field name on any IDFObject raises InvalidFieldError instead of returning None, and assigning a value the schema refuses raises ValidationFailedError, as add() does.

    		 True
    preserve_formatting bool

    When True, store the raw JSON text so that write_epjson and save_epjson can reproduce it byte-for-byte when no objects have been modified.

    		 False
    normalize_choices bool

    When True (the default), each choice value is stored in the spelling its schema declares, whatever case the file used: a surface the file calls WALL has surface_type == "Wall", as its Literal type says, so an exhaustive match holds on models you did not write. EnergyPlus reads choices case-insensitively, so no simulation changes. False keeps the file's text, and a choice field's Literal type then does not hold; see IDFDocument.normalize_choices.

    		 True

    Returns:

    Type Description
    AnyIDFDocument

    The parsed document: an AnyIDFDocument, or typed as as_type= or the
    AnyIDFDocument

    since=/before= range when one is given.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    IDFParseError

    For an object type the schema does not have, with strict_parsing.
    TypeError

    As load_idf raises it.
    ValueError

    As load_idf raises it.

    Examples:

    Load an epJSON model and iterate over zones:

    ```python
model = load_epjson("SmallOffice.epJSON")
for zone in model["Zone"]:
    print(zone.name, zone.x_origin)
```

    Load it typed for the release it must be:

    ```python
from idfkit.versioned import IDFDocumentV24_1

model = load_epjson("SmallOffice.epJSON", as_type=IDFDocumentV24_1)
```

    Specify an explicit EnergyPlus version:

    ```python
model = load_epjson("SmallOffice.epJSON", version=(24, 1, 0))
```

    def load_epjson(
    path: Path | str,
    version: tuple[int, int, int] | None = None,
    *,
    as_type: DocumentTypeTarget | None = None,
    since: ReleaseBound | None = None,
    before: ReleaseBound | None = None,
    strict_parsing: bool = True,
    strict: bool = True,
    preserve_formatting: bool = False,
    normalize_choices: bool = True,
) -> AnyIDFDocument:
    """
    Load an epJSON file and return its document.

    The document is typed as ``AnyIDFDocument`` unless ``as_type=``, ``since=`` or ``before=``
    names its release, as for [load_idf][idfkit.load_idf].

    Args:
        path: Path to the epJSON file
        version: Optional version override (major, minor, patch)
        as_type: The document type of the release the file must be, or a tuple of them, as for
            [load_idf][idfkit.load_idf].
        since: The first release of a range the file must be in, as for [load_idf][idfkit.load_idf].
        before: The release that range stops before, as for [load_idf][idfkit.load_idf].
        strict_parsing: When ``True`` (the default), an object type the schema does not
            have raises [IDFParseError][idfkit.exceptions.IDFParseError], as [load_idf][idfkit.load_idf] does,
            and the message suggests the closest type; EnergyPlus refuses such a file. ``False``
            skips it with a logged warning.
        strict: When ``True``, accessing or setting an unknown field name on any
            IDFObject raises [InvalidFieldError][idfkit.exceptions.InvalidFieldError] instead
            of returning ``None``, and assigning a value the schema refuses raises
            [ValidationFailedError][idfkit.exceptions.ValidationFailedError], as ``add()`` does.
        preserve_formatting: When ``True``, store the raw JSON text so
            that [write_epjson][idfkit.writers.write_epjson] and [save_epjson][idfkit.writers.save_epjson] can
            reproduce it byte-for-byte
            when no objects have been modified.
        normalize_choices: When ``True`` (the default), each choice value is stored in the
            spelling its schema declares, whatever case the file used: a surface the file
            calls ``WALL`` has ``surface_type == "Wall"``, as its ``Literal`` type says, so an
            exhaustive ``match`` holds on models you did not write. EnergyPlus reads choices
            case-insensitively, so no simulation changes. ``False`` keeps the file's text, and
            a choice field's ``Literal`` type then does not hold; see
            [IDFDocument.normalize_choices][idfkit.document.IDFDocument.normalize_choices].

    Returns:
        The parsed document: an ``AnyIDFDocument``, or typed as ``as_type=`` or the
        ``since=``/``before=`` range when one is given.

    Raises:
        IDFParseError: For an object type the schema does not have, with *strict_parsing*.
        TypeError: As [load_idf][idfkit.load_idf] raises it.
        ValueError: As [load_idf][idfkit.load_idf] raises it.

    Examples:
        Load an epJSON model and iterate over zones:

            ```python
            model = load_epjson("SmallOffice.epJSON")
            for zone in model["Zone"]:
                print(zone.name, zone.x_origin)
            ```

        Load it typed for the release it must be:

            ```python
            from idfkit.versioned import IDFDocumentV24_1

            model = load_epjson("SmallOffice.epJSON", as_type=IDFDocumentV24_1)
            ```

        Specify an explicit EnergyPlus version:

            ```python
            model = load_epjson("SmallOffice.epJSON", version=(24, 1, 0))
            ```
    """
    strict = _prepare(as_type, since, before, strict, version)
    doc = parse_epjson(
        Path(path),
        version=version,
        strict=strict,
        strict_parsing=strict_parsing,
        preserve_formatting=preserve_formatting,
        normalize_choices=normalize_choices,
    )
    return _narrow(doc, path, as_type, since, before)

    IDF Parser¶

    Streaming IDF parser - parses EnergyPlus IDF files into IDFDocument.

    Features: - Memory-efficient streaming for large files - Regex-based tokenization - Direct parsing into IDFDocument (no intermediate structures) - Type coercion based on schema - Optional CST (Concrete Syntax Tree) for lossless round-tripping

    logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) module-attribute ¶

    IDFParser ¶

    Streaming parser for IDF files.

    Uses memory mapping for large files and regex for tokenization.

    class IDFParser:
    """
    Streaming parser for IDF files.

    Uses memory mapping for large files and regex for tokenization.
    """

    __slots__ = (
        "_content",
        "_diagnostics",
        "_encoding",
        "_filepath",
        "_normalize_choices",
        "_requested_encoding",
        "_schema",
        "_strict_parsing",
    )

    _filepath: Path
    _schema: EpJSONSchema | None
    #: The codec the parse in progress decodes with: the requested one, else the detected one.
    _encoding: str
    #: The codec the caller asked for, or ``None`` to detect it from each file's bytes.
    _requested_encoding: str | None
    _content: bytes | None
    _strict_parsing: bool
    _diagnostics: list[ParseDiagnostic]
    #: Whether the parse in progress stores choices in their schema's spelling; set by
    #: [parse][idfkit.idf_parser.IDFParser.parse].
    _normalize_choices: bool

    def __init__(
        self,
        filepath: Path,
        schema: EpJSONSchema | None = None,
        encoding: str | None = None,
        strict_parsing: bool = True,
    ):
        self._filepath = filepath
        self._schema = schema
        self._requested_encoding = encoding
        self._encoding = encoding or "latin-1"
        self._strict_parsing = strict_parsing
        self._normalize_choices = True
        self._content: bytes | None = None
        # Recoverable findings from the last parse: the ones that did not stop it.
        #
        # These have always been produced; they went to the logging module and nowhere else, so a
        # caller who wanted them had to install a handler before parsing. They are collected here
        # too, so `load_idf_with_diagnostics` can hand them back in one call. Every logging
        # announcement still fires exactly as it did (FR-014); this adds a second way to reach the
        # same findings and removes none.
        self._diagnostics = []

    @property
    def diagnostics(self) -> tuple[ParseDiagnostic, ...]:
        """Recoverable findings from the most recent parse, in the order they were noticed."""
        return tuple(self._diagnostics)

    def _record(
        self,
        message: str,
        *,
        code: ParseDiagnosticCode,
        obj_type: str | None = None,
        obj_name: str | None = None,
        content: bytes | None = None,
        offset: int | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Note a recoverable finding, resolving its position while the offset is still in hand.

        The position has to be captured here rather than recovered later. The aggregate site used
        to reduce its findings to a set of type names before warning, which threw away every offset
        it had, and a finding with no position is not the finding the other language returns.
        """
        line: int | None = None
        column: int | None = None
        if content is not None and offset is not None:
            line, column = self._line_and_column(content, offset)
        self._diagnostics.append(
            ParseDiagnostic(
                message=message,
                filepath=str(self._filepath),
                obj_type=obj_type,
                obj_name=obj_name,
                line=line,
                column=column,
                code=code,
            )
        )

    def parse(
        self,
        version: tuple[int, int, int] | None = None,
        *,
        strict: bool = True,
        preserve_formatting: bool = False,
        normalize_choices: bool = True,
    ) -> IDFDocument:
        """
        Parse the IDF file into an IDFDocument.

        Args:
            version: Optional version override
            strict: Enforce strict field access on the resulting document.
            preserve_formatting: Build a CST for lossless round-tripping.
            normalize_choices: Store each choice value in the spelling its schema declares.

        Returns:
            Parsed IDFDocument
        """
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        # A parser may be reused, and findings belong to one parse rather than to its whole life.
        self._diagnostics = []
        self._normalize_choices = normalize_choices
        logger.debug("Parsing IDF file %s", self._filepath)

        # Load content (with mmap for large files)
        content, self._encoding, source_encoding = _resolve_encoding(self._load_content(), self._requested_encoding)
        if _EPJSON_START.match(content):
            raise FileFormatError(str(self._filepath), "epjson")

        # Detect version if not provided
        if version is None:
            version = self._detect_version(content)
            logger.debug("Detected version %d.%d.%d", *version)

        # Load schema if not provided
        schema = self._schema
        if schema is None:
            from .schema import get_schema

            schema = get_schema(version)

        # Create document
        doc = IDFDocument(
            version=version,
            schema=schema,
            filepath=self._filepath,
            strict=strict,
            normalize_choices=normalize_choices,
        )
        doc._source_encoding = source_encoding
        doc._source_newline = _detect_newline(content)

        # Parse objects
        self._parse_objects(content, doc, schema)

        # Build CST for lossless round-tripping (opt-in, no cost when False)
        if preserve_formatting:
            original_text = content.decode(self._encoding)
            cst = _build_idf_cst(original_text)
            cst.encoding = source_encoding
            if _link_cst_to_objects(cst, doc, self._diagnostics, str(self._filepath)):
                doc._cst = cst  # pyright: ignore[reportAttributeAccessIssue]
                doc._raw_text = original_text  # pyright: ignore[reportAttributeAccessIssue]
            else:
                logger.warning("CST discarded due to linking failure — lossless round-trip disabled")
                # No position: the failure is a property of the whole tree, not of one place in it.
                self._record(
                    "CST discarded due to linking failure, lossless round-trip disabled",
                    code="ParseError",
                )

        elapsed = time.perf_counter() - t0
        logger.info("Parsed %d objects from %s in %.3fs", len(doc), self._filepath, elapsed)

        return doc

    def _load_content(self) -> bytes:
        """Load file content, using mmap for large files."""
        file_size = self._filepath.stat().st_size
        use_mmap = file_size > _MMAP_THRESHOLD

        if use_mmap:
            logger.debug("Using mmap for large file (%d bytes)", file_size)
            # Use memory mapping for large files
            with open(self._filepath, "rb") as f:
                mm = mmap.mmap(f.fileno(), 0, access=mmap.ACCESS_READ)
                content = bytes(mm)
                mm.close()
        else:
            with open(self._filepath, "rb") as f:
                content = f.read()

        return content

    def _detect_version(self, content: bytes) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
        """Detect EnergyPlus version from file content."""
        # Search the whole file. ``content`` is already in memory, so a window
        # saves nothing here and costs correctness: nothing in the format puts
        # the Version object near the top, and three of the example files
        # shipped with EnergyPlus 26.1.0 carry it past the first 10 KB.
        match = _search_version(content)
        if match:
            major = int(match.group(1))
            minor = int(match.group(2))
            patch = int(match.group(3)) if match.group(3) else 0
            return (major, minor, patch)

        raise VersionNotFoundError(str(self._filepath))

    def _parse_objects(
        self,
        content: bytes,
        doc: AnyIDFDocument,
        schema: EpJSONSchema | None,
    ) -> None:
        """Parse all objects from content into document."""
        # Strip comments before matching to prevent phantom objects
        # (e.g. "!- X,Y,Z Origin" matching "X," as an object type)
        content = _COMMENT_PATTERN.sub(b"", content)

        # Local per-type caches avoid repeated schema lookups
        type_cache: dict[str, ParsingCache | None] = {}
        canonical_cache: dict[str, str] = {}
        encoding = self._encoding
        # Values are normalized while the fields are read, so objects are filed as they are.
        addidfobject = doc._adopt  # pyright: ignore[reportPrivateUsage]
        skipped_types: set[str] = set()

        # Every match ends at a `;`, so nothing past the last one can match. Bounding the scan there
        # keeps the scanner off the unterminated tail, which is reported on its own below.
        end = content.rfind(b";") + 1

        for match in _OBJECT_PATTERN.finditer(content, 0, end):
            match_offset = match.start(1)
            obj_type: str | None = None
            obj_name: str | None = None

            try:
                decoded_obj_type = match.group(1).decode(encoding).strip()
                obj_type = decoded_obj_type

                obj_name = self._extract_object_name(match, encoding)

                pc, should_skip, decoded_obj_type = self._resolve_type_cache(
                    content=content,
                    schema=schema,
                    type_cache=type_cache,
                    canonical_cache=canonical_cache,
                    skipped_types=skipped_types,
                    obj_type=decoded_obj_type,
                    obj_name=obj_name,
                    match_offset=match_offset,
                )
                if should_skip:
                    continue

                obj = self._parse_object_cached(match, pc, encoding, obj_type_override=decoded_obj_type, schema=schema)
                if obj:
                    addidfobject(obj)
            except IDFParseError:
                raise
            except Exception as exc:
                if self._strict_parsing:
                    self._raise_parse_error(
                        content,
                        match_offset,
                        f"Failed to parse object: {exc}",
                        obj_type=obj_type,
                        obj_name=obj_name,
                    )
                logger.warning("Skipping malformed object %r: %s", obj_type or "<decode_error>", exc)
                self._record(
                    f"Skipping malformed object: {exc}",
                    code="ParseError",
                    obj_type=obj_type,
                    obj_name=obj_name,
                    content=content,
                    offset=match_offset,
                )

        if skipped_types:
            logger.warning(
                "Skipped %d unknown object type(s): %s", len(skipped_types), ", ".join(sorted(skipped_types))
            )

        self._check_unterminated_tail(content, end, encoding)

    def _check_unterminated_tail(self, content: bytes, end: int, encoding: str) -> None:
        """Report text after the last ``;`` that is not blank, which is an object missing its ``;``.

        The object pattern only matches text that reaches a semicolon, so such an object used to be
        discarded without a word (idfkit#187). *content* has had its comments stripped already, so
        a trailing comment is blank here, and offsets still give the original line numbers.
        """
        tail = content[end:]
        stripped = tail.lstrip(_TRAILING_BLANK)
        if not stripped.rstrip(_TRAILING_BLANK):
            return

        offset = end + len(tail) - len(stripped)
        # A truncated file can end inside a multibyte character, so decoding must not raise here:
        # that would replace the finding with a UnicodeDecodeError, even on the returning path.
        type_match = _TAIL_TYPE_PATTERN.match(stripped)
        obj_type = type_match.group(1).decode(encoding, errors="replace").strip() if type_match else None
        # Only a few bytes per quoted character are needed; the tail may be most of the file.
        head = stripped[: _UNTERMINATED_EXCERPT * 8].decode(encoding, errors="replace")
        excerpt = " ".join(head.split())
        if len(excerpt) > _UNTERMINATED_EXCERPT or len(stripped) > _UNTERMINATED_EXCERPT * 8:
            excerpt = excerpt[:_UNTERMINATED_EXCERPT] + "..."
        message = f'Unterminated object near "{excerpt}" (missing ";")'

        if self._strict_parsing:
            self._raise_parse_error(content, offset, message, obj_type=obj_type)
        logger.warning("Skipping unterminated object %r: %s", obj_type or "<unknown>", message)
        self._record(message, code="ParseError", obj_type=obj_type, content=content, offset=offset)

    def _parse_object_cached(
        self,
        match: re.Match[bytes],
        pc: ParsingCache | None,
        encoding: str,
        *,
        obj_type_override: str | None = None,
        schema: EpJSONSchema | None = None,
    ) -> IDFObject | None:
        """Parse a single object from regex match using cached metadata.

        *schema* names the object types a value running onto the next line is checked against.
        """
        obj_type = obj_type_override or match.group(1).decode(encoding).strip()
        fields_raw = match.group(2).decode(encoding)

        fields = self._parse_fields(fields_raw)
        if not fields:
            return None

        swallowed: int | None = None
        if pc is not None and schema is not None and _VALUE_THEN_LINE_BREAK.search(fields_raw) is not None:
            swallowed = self._check_swallowed_object(match, fields_raw, encoding, obj_type, fields, pc, schema)

        if pc is not None:
            has_name = pc.has_name
            # Mutable copy since extensible parsing appends to it
            field_names: list[str] = list(pc.field_names) if has_name else list(pc.all_field_names)

            name, remaining_fields = (fields[0], fields[1:]) if has_name else ("", fields)

            invalid: list[tuple[int, str, str]] = []
            data = self._build_data_dict_cached(remaining_fields, field_names, pc, invalid)
            if invalid and swallowed is not None:
                # The values from the swallowed one on are the lost object's, read into this one's
                # fields; the missing ';' was reported once already, so they are not reported again.
                invalid = [entry for entry in invalid if entry[0] + (1 if has_name else 0) < swallowed]
            if invalid:
                self._report_invalid_fields(match, fields_raw, encoding, obj_type, fields, pc, invalid)

            return IDFObject(
                obj_type=obj_type,
                name=name,
                data=data,
                schema=pc.obj_schema,
                field_order=field_names,
                ref_fields=pc.ref_fields,
                extensibles=frozenset(pc.ext_field_names),
                wrapper_key=pc.ext_wrapper_key,
                ext_inner_names=tuple(pc.ext_inner_props.keys()),
                aliases=pc.field_aliases,
            )

        # No-schema fallback
        name = fields[0] if fields else ""
        remaining = fields[1:]
        data: dict[str, Any] = {}
        for i, value in enumerate(remaining):
            if value:
                data[f"field_{i + 1}"] = value
        return IDFObject(obj_type=obj_type, name=name, data=data)

    def _check_swallowed_object(
        self,
        match: re.Match[bytes],
        fields_raw: str,
        encoding: str,
        obj_type: str,
        fields: list[str],
        pc: ParsingCache,
        schema: EpJSONSchema,
    ) -> int | None:
        """Report a value that runs onto a line starting with an object type: a missing ``;``.

        ``Zone, A, 0, 0, 0`` followed by ``Material, M;`` reads as one Zone whose y origin is
        ``"0\nMaterial"``, and the Material is lost. The finding never stops the parse, in either mode:
        a line break inside a value is legal (``My`` then ``Zone,`` is the one name ``"My Zone"``), so
        the object is kept as read, a warning is logged, and a ``ParseError`` diagnostic is recorded,
        which [load_idf_with_diagnostics][idfkit.load_idf_with_diagnostics] returns.

        Returns the index in *fields* of the value reported, or ``None`` when there is none.
        """
        for index, value in enumerate(fields):
            if "\n" not in value:
                continue
            before, _, after = value.partition("\n")
            next_type = next((line.strip() for line in after.split("\n") if line.strip()), "")
            if schema.resolve_type_name(next_type) is None:
                continue
            field_name = _swallowed_field_name(pc, index)
            message = (
                f"Field {field_name!r} runs onto the next line, which starts with {next_type!r}: "
                f"missing ';' after {before.strip()!r}, before {next_type!r}?"
            )
            offset = _field_offset(fields_raw, index)
            prefix = 0 if offset is None else len(fields_raw[:offset].encode(encoding))
            position = match.start(2) + prefix
            # When the name itself ran on, the object's name is the part before the line break.
            obj_name = (before.strip() if index == 0 else fields[0]) if pc.has_name else None
            logger.warning("Possible missing ';' in %s %r: %s", obj_type, obj_name, message)
            self._record(
                message, code="ParseError", obj_type=obj_type, obj_name=obj_name, content=match.string, offset=position
            )
            return index
        return None

    def _report_invalid_fields(
        self,
        match: re.Match[bytes],
        fields_raw: str,
        encoding: str,
        obj_type: str,
        fields: list[str],
        pc: ParsingCache,
        invalid: list[tuple[int, str, str]],
    ) -> None:
        """Report values the schema declares numeric that are neither numeric nor a legal sentinel.

        Never raises, in either mode. A value of the wrong kind does not stop the parse: the object
        is built and the document is returned, so a caller who was reading strictly still gets what
        they got before (FR-014). The value is kept as read, so ``validate_document()`` reports it.
        This adds a finding where there was silence, and nothing else.

        The finding is positioned at the offending FIELD rather than at the object, because that is
        what makes it useful: the shape this catches is a missing semicolon swallowing the object
        below, and the object's own first line is nowhere near the damage.
        """
        name_offset = 1 if pc.has_name else 0
        for index, field_name, value in invalid:
            if _string_is_legal(pc.obj_schema, field_name, value):
                continue

            offset = _field_offset(fields_raw, index + name_offset)
            prefix = 0 if offset is None else len(fields_raw[:offset].encode(encoding))
            position = match.start(2) + prefix

            self._record(
                f"Field {field_name!r} expects a number, got {value!r}",
                code="InvalidField",
                obj_type=obj_type,
                obj_name=fields[0] if pc.has_name and fields else None,
                content=match.string,
                offset=position,
            )

    def _build_data_dict_cached(
        self,
        remaining_fields: list[str],
        field_names: list[str],
        pc: ParsingCache,
        invalid: list[tuple[int, str, str]] | None = None,
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Build the data dict using pre-computed field types from the cache.

        *invalid* collects ``(index, field name, value)`` for each value the schema declares numeric
        that did not coerce. It is almost always empty, and detecting that costs one identity test
        and one frozenset lookup per field: ``_coerce_value_fast`` returns a NEW object when it
        succeeds and hands back the very string it was given when it fails, so ``is`` separates the
        two without re-parsing anything.

        Whether such a value is actually wrong is not decided here. A numeric field routinely
        accepts ``autosize``; that question needs the schema and is asked on the reporting path.

        A value left a string is, when it folds to one of its field's choices, stored in the
        spelling the schema declares, so the field's ``Literal`` type holds for any file. The
        same identity test confines that lookup to strings: a coerced number never pays for it.
        """
        data: dict[str, Any] = {}
        field_types = pc.field_types
        num_named = len(field_names)
        choices = pc.choice_spellings if self._normalize_choices else None

        # zip stops at the named fields: the extensible tail is bucketed below, not walked here.
        for i, (field_name, value) in enumerate(zip(field_names, remaining_fields, strict=False)):
            # A blank field is unset and stays absent, as in epJSON and as the extensible groups below
            # already do. Holding it as "" made the model disagree with both writers, which drop it,
            # so a re-parse of idfkit's own output was not equal to the original (idfkit#183).
            if value:
                field_type = field_types.get(field_name)
                coerced = _coerce_value_fast(field_type, value)
                if coerced is value:
                    if invalid is not None and field_type in _NUMERIC_FIELD_TYPES:
                        invalid.append((i, field_name, value))
                    if choices and (table := choices.get(field_name)) is not None:
                        coerced = table.get(value.casefold(), value)
                data[field_name] = coerced

        if len(remaining_fields) > num_named:
            extra = remaining_fields[num_named:]
            if pc.extensible:
                self._append_extensible_fields(
                    data=data,
                    extra=extra,
                    field_names=field_names,
                    field_types=field_types,
                    pc=pc,
                )
            elif self._strict_parsing and any(extra):
                # Trailing blanks past the last field are unset, like any other blank field, and are
                # not extra values: EnergyPlus accepts ``Timestep,4,,;`` and refuses ``Timestep,4,5;``.
                # It is also how idfkit writes an object with nothing in it to keep its terminator,
                # ``GroundHeatTransfer:Slab:XFACE,;``. Only the values up to the last non-blank one
                # are counted as extra.
                overflow = len(extra) - next(i for i, value in enumerate(reversed(extra)) if value)
                msg = (
                    f"Object has {overflow} extra field(s) but type is not extensible "
                    f"(expected at most {num_named}, got {num_named + overflow})"
                )
                raise ValueError(msg)

        return data

    def _append_extensible_fields(
        self,
        *,
        data: dict[str, Any],
        extra: list[str],
        field_names: list[str],
        field_types: dict[str, str | None],
        pc: ParsingCache,
    ) -> None:
        """Bucket extensible-group tokens into a canonical wrapper array.

        Tokens are split into ``ext_size``-wide groups; each group becomes
        a dict keyed by the schema's inner property names, and the resulting
        list is stored under ``data[wrapper_key]`` (e.g. ``data["vertices"]``).
        The wrapper key is *not* added to ``field_names`` — the IDF writer
        handles wrapper expansion separately via the schema cache.
        """
        ext_size = pc.ext_size
        if ext_size <= 0:
            if self._strict_parsing:
                msg = "Object is marked extensible but extensible group size is invalid"
                raise ValueError(msg)
            return

        ext_names = pc.ext_field_names
        num_ext = len(ext_names)
        ext_types = tuple(field_types.get(name) for name in ext_names)
        wrapper_key = pc.ext_wrapper_key
        ext_choices = pc.ext_choice_spellings if self._normalize_choices else None

        items: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        for group_start in range(0, len(extra), ext_size):
            group = extra[group_start : group_start + ext_size]
            # A blank slot is absent rather than "", as in epJSON; the IDF writer restores it (idfkit#182).
            item: dict[str, Any] = {
                ext_names[j]: _coerce_value_fast(ext_types[j], value)
                for j, value in enumerate(group[:num_ext])
                if value
            }
            # Drop all-empty groups (e.g. an extra "," at the end of the extensible block).
            # Keeping them would emit phantom vertices.
            if item:
                if ext_choices:
                    for name, value in item.items():
                        table = ext_choices.get(name)
                        if table is not None and type(value) is str:
                            item[name] = table.get(value.casefold(), value)
                items.append(item)

        if items and wrapper_key is not None:
            data[wrapper_key] = items

    def _parse_fields(self, fields_raw: str) -> list[str]:
        """Parse and clean field values from raw string."""
        # Fast path: comments already stripped by _COMMENT_PATTERN in _parse_objects
        if "!" not in fields_raw:
            return [part.strip() for part in fields_raw.split(",")]

        # Slow path: strip inline comments (safety fallback)
        lines: list[str] = []
        for line in fields_raw.split("\n"):
            idx = line.find("!")
            if idx >= 0:
                line = line[:idx]
            lines.append(line)
        clean_text = " ".join(lines)
        return [part.strip() for part in clean_text.split(",")]

    @staticmethod
    def _line_and_column(content: bytes, offset: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
        """Convert a byte offset to 1-based (line, column)."""
        line = content.count(b"\n", 0, offset) + 1
        previous_newline = content.rfind(b"\n", 0, offset)
        if previous_newline < 0:
            return (line, offset + 1)
        return (line, offset - previous_newline)

    @staticmethod
    def _extract_object_name(match: re.Match[bytes], encoding: str) -> str | None:
        """Best-effort extraction of the raw first field (typically object name)."""
        fields_raw = match.group(2).decode(encoding)
        first = fields_raw.split(",", maxsplit=1)[0].strip()
        return first or None

    def _raise_parse_error(
        self,
        content: bytes,
        offset: int,
        message: str,
        *,
        obj_type: str | None = None,
        obj_name: str | None = None,
        code: ParseDiagnosticCode = "ParseError",
    ) -> None:
        """Raise a ParseError with contextual diagnostics."""
        line, column = self._line_and_column(content, offset)
        diagnostic = ParseDiagnostic(
            message=message,
            filepath=str(self._filepath),
            obj_type=obj_type,
            obj_name=obj_name,
            line=line,
            column=column,
            code=code,
        )
        summary = "Failed to parse IDF"
        raise IDFParseError(summary, diagnostics=[diagnostic])

    def _resolve_type_cache(
        self,
        *,
        content: bytes,
        schema: EpJSONSchema | None,
        type_cache: dict[str, ParsingCache | None],
        canonical_cache: dict[str, str],
        skipped_types: set[str],
        obj_type: str,
        obj_name: str | None,
        match_offset: int,
    ) -> tuple[ParsingCache | None, bool, str]:
        """Resolve and cache parsing metadata for an object type.

        Returns ``(cache, should_skip, canonical_type)`` where *canonical_type*
        is the PascalCase schema name (may differ from the raw IDF casing).
        """
        if schema is None:
            return (None, False, obj_type)

        pc = type_cache.get(obj_type)
        if pc is None and obj_type not in type_cache:
            pc = schema.get_parsing_cache(obj_type)
            type_cache[obj_type] = pc

        if pc is not None:
            # Return cached canonical name (resolved once per raw type).
            canonical = canonical_cache.get(obj_type)
            if canonical is None:
                canonical = schema.resolve_type_name(obj_type) or obj_type
                canonical_cache[obj_type] = canonical
            return (pc, False, canonical)

        if self._strict_parsing:
            # The same code the recoverable path below uses, and the same one the other language
            # reports for this input. A finding must not change kind depending on which mode was
            # asked for: it is the same finding, arriving on a different path.
            msg = f"Unknown object type '{obj_type}'"
            self._raise_parse_error(
                content,
                match_offset,
                msg,
                obj_type=obj_type,
                obj_name=obj_name,
                code="UnknownObjectType",
            )

        # One finding per skip, positioned, and recorded HERE rather than after the loop.
        #
        # `skipped_types` is a set and stays one, because the log line it feeds is a summary and
        # changing it would change what an existing caller sees. But a set of type names is not
        # what the other language returns: it collapses four skips of the same type into one and
        # discards every offset. The offset is in hand at exactly this point and nowhere later,
        # which is why the finding is built here.
        self._record(
            f"Unknown object type '{obj_type}'",
            code="UnknownObjectType",
            obj_type=obj_type,
            obj_name=obj_name,
            content=content,
            offset=match_offset,
        )
        skipped_types.add(obj_type)
        return (None, True, obj_type)

    def parse(
    self,
    version: tuple[int, int, int] | None = None,
    *,
    strict: bool = True,
    preserve_formatting: bool = False,
    normalize_choices: bool = True,
) -> IDFDocument:
    """
    Parse the IDF file into an IDFDocument.

    Args:
        version: Optional version override
        strict: Enforce strict field access on the resulting document.
        preserve_formatting: Build a CST for lossless round-tripping.
        normalize_choices: Store each choice value in the spelling its schema declares.

    Returns:
        Parsed IDFDocument
    """
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    # A parser may be reused, and findings belong to one parse rather than to its whole life.
    self._diagnostics = []
    self._normalize_choices = normalize_choices
    logger.debug("Parsing IDF file %s", self._filepath)

    # Load content (with mmap for large files)
    content, self._encoding, source_encoding = _resolve_encoding(self._load_content(), self._requested_encoding)
    if _EPJSON_START.match(content):
        raise FileFormatError(str(self._filepath), "epjson")

    # Detect version if not provided
    if version is None:
        version = self._detect_version(content)
        logger.debug("Detected version %d.%d.%d", *version)

    # Load schema if not provided
    schema = self._schema
    if schema is None:
        from .schema import get_schema

        schema = get_schema(version)

    # Create document
    doc = IDFDocument(
        version=version,
        schema=schema,
        filepath=self._filepath,
        strict=strict,
        normalize_choices=normalize_choices,
    )
    doc._source_encoding = source_encoding
    doc._source_newline = _detect_newline(content)

    # Parse objects
    self._parse_objects(content, doc, schema)

    # Build CST for lossless round-tripping (opt-in, no cost when False)
    if preserve_formatting:
        original_text = content.decode(self._encoding)
        cst = _build_idf_cst(original_text)
        cst.encoding = source_encoding
        if _link_cst_to_objects(cst, doc, self._diagnostics, str(self._filepath)):
            doc._cst = cst  # pyright: ignore[reportAttributeAccessIssue]
            doc._raw_text = original_text  # pyright: ignore[reportAttributeAccessIssue]
        else:
            logger.warning("CST discarded due to linking failure — lossless round-trip disabled")
            # No position: the failure is a property of the whole tree, not of one place in it.
            self._record(
                "CST discarded due to linking failure, lossless round-trip disabled",
                code="ParseError",
            )

    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - t0
    logger.info("Parsed %d objects from %s in %.3fs", len(doc), self._filepath, elapsed)

    return doc

    Bases: Generic[_DocT]

    A document, and the recoverable findings from the parse that produced it.

    What load_idf_with_diagnostics hands back. The findings here are the ones that did NOT stop the parse: a skipped unknown type, a malformed object, a formatting tree that could not be linked. The ones that did stop it never reach this type, because there is no document to pair them with; they arrive on IDFParseError.diagnostics instead.

    Field names match the other language's ParseResult exactly, so a reader moving between the two reads the same two names in the same order.

    Generic in the document's type: ParseResult alone carries an AnyIDFDocument, since a file's release is known only once it is read, and load_idf_with_diagnostics(path, as_type=IDFDocumentV9_4) returns a ParseResult[IDFDocumentV9_4].

    def get_idf_version(filepath: Path | str) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
    """
    Quick version detection without full parsing.

    Reads the first 10 KB of the file, which holds the ``Version`` object in
    almost every model, and falls back to reading the rest only when it does
    not. The common case costs one small read; no valid file is refused for
    stating its version late. Nothing in the IDF format requires ``Version``
    to appear near the top, and three of the example files shipped with
    EnergyPlus 26.1.0 carry it past 10 KB.

    Args:
        filepath: Path to IDF file

    Returns:
        Version tuple (major, minor, patch)

    Raises:
        VersionNotFoundError: If the file holds no Version object

    Examples:
        Check which EnergyPlus version a model was created for
        (usually reads only the first 10 KB):

            ```python
            from idfkit import get_idf_version

            version = get_idf_version("5ZoneAirCooled.idf")
            print(f"EnergyPlus v{version[0]}.{version[1]}.{version[2]}")
            ```
    """
    filepath = Path(filepath)

    with open(filepath, "rb") as f:
        head = f.read(_VERSION_SCAN_BYTES)
        # A comment's `!` precedes its text, so the window holds it whenever it holds the text.
        match = _search_version(head)
        if match is None:
            # The scan window may have split the Version object, so re-search
            # the whole file rather than only the remainder.
            match = _search_version(head + f.read())

    if match:
        major = int(match.group(1))
        minor = int(match.group(2))
        patch = int(match.group(3)) if match.group(3) else 0
        return (major, minor, patch)

    raise VersionNotFoundError(str(filepath))

    def iter_idf_objects(
    filepath: Path | str,
    encoding: str | None = None,
) -> Iterator[tuple[str, str, list[str]]]:
    """
    Iterate over objects in an IDF file without loading into document.

    Yields:
        Tuples of (object_type, name, [field_values])

    This is useful for quick scanning or filtering without full parsing.
    ``encoding`` is read as [parse_idf][idfkit.idf_parser.parse_idf] reads it: ``None`` detects UTF-8 or latin-1.

    Note:
        Type names are returned exactly as they appear in the IDF file
        (no schema-based case normalization).  Use case-insensitive
        comparisons when filtering: ``obj_type.upper() == "ZONE"``.

    Examples:
        Count thermal zones without loading the full document
        (useful for quickly sizing batch runs):

            ```python
            from idfkit import iter_idf_objects

            zone_count = sum(
                1 for obj_type, name, _
                in iter_idf_objects("5ZoneAirCooled.idf")
                if obj_type == "Zone"
            )
            ```

        Collect all material names for an audit report:

            ```python
            materials = [
                name for obj_type, name, _
                in iter_idf_objects("LargeOffice.idf")
                if obj_type == "Material"
            ]
            ```
    """
    filepath = Path(filepath)

    with open(filepath, "rb") as f:
        content = f.read()
    content, encoding, _ = _resolve_encoding(content, encoding)

    # Strip comments before matching to prevent phantom objects
    content = _COMMENT_PATTERN.sub(b"", content)

    # As in `IDFParser._parse_objects`: no match reaches past the last `;`, and scanning an
    # unterminated tail costs time quadratic in its length for nothing (idfkit#187).
    end = content.rfind(b";") + 1
    if content[end:].strip(_TRAILING_BLANK):
        logger.warning('Ignoring unterminated object at the end of %s (missing ";")', filepath)

    for match in _OBJECT_PATTERN.finditer(content, 0, end):
        obj_type = match.group(1).decode(encoding).strip()
        fields_raw = match.group(2).decode(encoding)

        # Split and clean fields
        fields: list[str] = []
        for part in fields_raw.split(","):
            if "!" in part:
                part = part[: part.index("!")]
            fields.append(part.strip())

        obj_name = fields[0] if fields else ""
        yield (obj_type, obj_name, fields[1:])

    parse_idf(filepath, schema=None, version=None, encoding=None, strict_parsing=True, strict=True, *, preserve_formatting=False, normalize_choices=True) ¶

    Parse an IDF file into an IDFDocument.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    filepath Path | str

    Path to the IDF file

    		 required
    schema EpJSONSchema | None

    Optional EpJSONSchema for field ordering and type coercion

    		 None
    version tuple[int, int, int] | None

    Optional version override (auto-detected if not provided)

    		 None
    encoding str | None

    File encoding. None (the default) reads the file as UTF-8 when its bytes are valid UTF-8, and as latin-1 otherwise. A leading UTF-8 byte-order mark is dropped. The document remembers the encoding, and save_idf writes it back unless told otherwise.

    		 None
    strict_parsing bool

    If True, fail fast on malformed objects (default: True)

    		 True
    strict bool

    When True, accessing or setting an unknown field name on any IDFObject raises InvalidFieldError instead of returning None, and assigning a value the schema refuses raises ValidationFailedError, as add() does.

    		 True
    preserve_formatting bool

    If True, build a Concrete Syntax Tree (CST) so that writing the document back preserves original formatting, comments, and whitespace for unmodified objects. The default code path is unchanged — no performance penalty when False.

    		 False
    normalize_choices bool

    When True (the default), each choice value is stored in the spelling its schema declares, whatever case the file used: WALL reads back "Wall", as the field's Literal type says. False keeps the file's text. Either way, a preserve_formatting=True write emits unmodified objects verbatim.

    		 True

    Returns:

    Type Description
    IDFDocument

    Parsed IDFDocument

    Raises:

    Type Description
    VersionNotFoundError

    If version cannot be detected
    IdfKitError

    If parsing fails

    Examples:

    Load and inspect a DOE reference building:

    ```python
from idfkit import parse_idf

model = parse_idf("RefBldgSmallOfficeNew2004.idf")
for zone in model["Zone"]:
    print(zone.name, zone.x_origin)
```

    Force a specific EnergyPlus version when auto-detection fails (e.g., a pre-v8.9 file that was manually upgraded):

    ```python
model = parse_idf("legacy_building.idf", version=(9, 6, 0))
```

    Round-trip an IDF file losslessly:

    ```python
model = parse_idf("building.idf", preserve_formatting=True)
# write_idf(model) reproduces the original byte-for-byte
```

) -> IDFDocument:
    """
    Parse an IDF file into an IDFDocument.

    Args:
        filepath: Path to the IDF file
        schema: Optional EpJSONSchema for field ordering and type coercion
        version: Optional version override (auto-detected if not provided)
        encoding: File encoding. ``None`` (the default) reads the file as UTF-8 when its bytes
            are valid UTF-8, and as latin-1 otherwise. A leading UTF-8 byte-order mark is dropped.
            The document remembers the encoding, and [save_idf][idfkit.writers.save_idf] writes it
            back unless told otherwise.
        strict_parsing: If True, fail fast on malformed objects (default: True)
        strict: When ``True``, accessing or setting an unknown field name on any
            IDFObject raises [InvalidFieldError][idfkit.exceptions.InvalidFieldError] instead
            of returning ``None``, and assigning a value the schema refuses raises
            [ValidationFailedError][idfkit.exceptions.ValidationFailedError], as ``add()`` does.
        preserve_formatting: If ``True``, build a Concrete Syntax Tree (CST)
            so that writing the document back preserves original formatting,
            comments, and whitespace for unmodified objects.  The default
            code path is unchanged — no performance penalty when ``False``.
        normalize_choices: When ``True`` (the default), each choice value is stored in the
            spelling its schema declares, whatever case the file used: ``WALL`` reads back
            ``"Wall"``, as the field's ``Literal`` type says. ``False`` keeps the file's text.
            Either way, a ``preserve_formatting=True`` write emits unmodified objects verbatim.

    Returns:
        Parsed IDFDocument

    Raises:
        VersionNotFoundError: If version cannot be detected
        IdfKitError: If parsing fails

    Examples:
        Load and inspect a DOE reference building:

            ```python
            from idfkit import parse_idf

            model = parse_idf("RefBldgSmallOfficeNew2004.idf")
            for zone in model["Zone"]:
                print(zone.name, zone.x_origin)
            ```

        Force a specific EnergyPlus version when auto-detection fails
        (e.g., a pre-v8.9 file that was manually upgraded):

            ```python
            model = parse_idf("legacy_building.idf", version=(9, 6, 0))
            ```

        Round-trip an IDF file losslessly:

            ```python
            model = parse_idf("building.idf", preserve_formatting=True)
            # write_idf(model) reproduces the original byte-for-byte
            ```
    """
    filepath = Path(filepath)

    if not filepath.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"IDF file not found: {filepath}")  # noqa: TRY003

    parser = IDFParser(filepath, schema, encoding, strict_parsing=strict_parsing)
    return parser.parse(
        version, strict=strict, preserve_formatting=preserve_formatting, normalize_choices=normalize_choices
    )

    parse_idf_with_diagnostics(filepath, schema=None, version=None, encoding=None, *, strict=True, preserve_formatting=False, normalize_choices=True) ¶

    Parse an IDF file, keeping the findings that did not stop the parse.

    The same work parse_idf(..., strict_parsing=False) does, handing back the recoverable findings alongside the document instead of only announcing them through the logging module.

    strict_parsing is not a parameter: a strict parse has no recoverable findings by definition, so this function always parses non-strictly. Findings that stop a parse still raise, and still arrive on IDFParseError.diagnostics.

    Every logging announcement fires exactly as it does today. A caller with a handler installed sees no change (FR-014); this is a second way to reach the same findings, not a replacement.

    def parse_idf_with_diagnostics(
    filepath: Path | str,
    schema: EpJSONSchema | None = None,
    version: tuple[int, int, int] | None = None,
    encoding: str | None = None,
    *,
    strict: bool = True,
    preserve_formatting: bool = False,
    normalize_choices: bool = True,
) -> ParseResult[IDFDocument]:
    """Parse an IDF file, keeping the findings that did not stop the parse.

    The same work `parse_idf(..., strict_parsing=False)` does, handing back the recoverable
    findings alongside the document instead of only announcing them through the logging module.

    `strict_parsing` is not a parameter: a strict parse has no recoverable findings by definition,
    so this function always parses non-strictly. Findings that stop a parse still raise, and still
    arrive on `IDFParseError.diagnostics`.

    Every logging announcement fires exactly as it does today. A caller with a handler installed
    sees no change (FR-014); this is a second way to reach the same findings, not a replacement.

    `encoding` and `normalize_choices` are the parameters of [parse_idf][idfkit.idf_parser.parse_idf].
    """
    filepath = Path(filepath)

    if not filepath.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"IDF file not found: {filepath}")  # noqa: TRY003

    parser = IDFParser(filepath, schema, encoding, strict_parsing=False)
    document = parser.parse(
        version, strict=strict, preserve_formatting=preserve_formatting, normalize_choices=normalize_choices
    )
    return ParseResult(document=document, diagnostics=parser.diagnostics)

    class EpJSONParser:
    """
    Parser for epJSON files.

    epJSON is the native JSON format for EnergyPlus models, making
    parsing straightforward - just json.load() and transform.
    """

    __slots__ = ("_filepath", "_schema")

    def __init__(
        self,
        filepath: Path,
        schema: EpJSONSchema | None = None,
    ):
        self._filepath = filepath
        self._schema = schema

    def parse(
        self,
        version: tuple[int, int, int] | None = None,
        *,
        strict: bool = True,
        strict_parsing: bool = True,
        preserve_formatting: bool = False,
        normalize_choices: bool = True,
    ) -> IDFDocument:
        """
        Parse the epJSON file into an IDFDocument.

        Args:
            version: Optional version override
            strict: Enforce strict field access on the resulting document.
            strict_parsing: Raise on an object type the schema does not have, rather than skip it.
            preserve_formatting: Store raw JSON text for lossless round-tripping.
            normalize_choices: Store each choice value in the spelling its schema declares.

        Returns:
            Parsed IDFDocument
        """
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        logger.debug("Parsing epJSON file %s", self._filepath)

        # Load JSON
        try:
            with open(self._filepath, encoding="utf-8") as f:
                raw_text = f.read()
            data: dict[str, Any] = json.loads(raw_text, parse_constant=_constant_refuser(self._filepath))
        except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
            # IDF text starts with a comment or an object type, never with '{'. An IDF file is often
            # latin-1 (save_idf's default) and so not UTF-8 at all: look at the bytes, not the text.
            with open(self._filepath, "rb") as f:
                head = f.read(4096)
            first = head.removeprefix(b"\xef\xbb\xbf").lstrip(b" \t\r\n")[:1]
            if first == b"!" or first.isalpha():
                raise FileFormatError(str(self._filepath), "idf") from exc
            raise

        # Detect version if not provided
        if version is None:
            version = self._detect_version(data)
            logger.debug("Detected version %d.%d.%d", *version)

        # Load schema if not provided
        schema = self._schema
        if schema is None:
            from .schema import get_schema

            schema = get_schema(version)

        # Create document
        doc = IDFDocument(
            version=version,
            schema=schema,
            filepath=self._filepath,
            strict=strict,
            normalize_choices=normalize_choices,
        )

        # Parse objects
        self._parse_objects(data, doc, schema, strict_parsing=strict_parsing, normalize_choices=normalize_choices)

        # Store raw text for lossless round-tripping (opt-in).
        if preserve_formatting:
            doc._raw_text = raw_text  # pyright: ignore[reportAttributeAccessIssue]
            # Mark all objects as "pristine" with a sentinel source_text so
            # that the writer can detect mutations.
            for obj in doc.all_objects:
                object.__setattr__(obj, "_source_text", "")
            # How many there were, so that a removal is visible to the writer.
            # The sentinel above only marks the objects that are still here, and
            # a removed one is not among them to ask.
            doc._count_at_read = len(doc)

        elapsed = time.perf_counter() - t0
        logger.info("Parsed %d objects from %s in %.3fs", len(doc), self._filepath, elapsed)

        return doc

    def _detect_version(self, data: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
        """Detect EnergyPlus version from epJSON data."""
        # Version is in the "Version" object
        version_obj = data.get("Version")

        if version_obj:
            # epJSON format: {"Version": {"Version 1": {"version_identifier": "23.2"}}}
            for _name, fields in version_obj.items():
                version_str: str = fields.get("version_identifier", "")
                if version_str:
                    return self._parse_version_string(version_str)

        raise VersionNotFoundError(str(self._filepath))

    @staticmethod
    def _parse_version_string(version_str: str) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
        """Parse version string like '23.2' or '9.2.0'."""
        parts = version_str.split(".")
        major = int(parts[0]) if len(parts) > 0 else 0
        minor = int(parts[1]) if len(parts) > 1 else 0
        patch = int(parts[2]) if len(parts) > 2 else 0
        return (major, minor, patch)

    def _parse_objects(
        self,
        data: dict[str, Any],
        doc: AnyIDFDocument,
        schema: EpJSONSchema | None,
        *,
        strict_parsing: bool = True,
        normalize_choices: bool = True,
    ) -> None:
        """Parse all objects from epJSON data into document.

        An object type *schema* does not have raises with *strict_parsing*, and is skipped
        without, as the IDF parser treats one.

        With *normalize_choices*, each choice is stored in the spelling its schema declares, as the
        IDF parser stores it. EnergyPlus's own epJSON is already canonical; a hand-written or
        converted file need not be.
        """
        # Values are normalized below while each object is built, so objects are filed as they are.
        addidfobject = doc._adopt  # pyright: ignore[reportPrivateUsage]
        unknown_fields: list[ParseDiagnostic] = []

        for obj_type, objects in data.items():
            if not isinstance(objects, dict):
                continue

            # Get schema info from parsing cache
            pc: ParsingCache | None = None
            obj_schema: dict[str, Any] | None = None
            base_field_names: tuple[str, ...] | None = None
            ref_fields: frozenset[str] | None = None
            has_name = True
            # epJSON format: {"ObjectType": {"obj_name": {fields...}, ...}}
            objects_dict = cast(dict[str, Any], objects)
            if schema:
                pc = schema.get_parsing_cache(obj_type)
                if pc is None:
                    self._unknown_type(obj_type, objects_dict, schema, strict_parsing=strict_parsing)
                    continue
                obj_schema = pc.obj_schema
                has_name = pc.has_name
                base_field_names = pc.field_names if has_name else pc.all_field_names
                ref_fields = pc.ref_fields

            for obj_name, fields in objects_dict.items():
                if not isinstance(fields, dict):
                    continue

                # Nameless objects: use empty string instead of epJSON dict key
                name = obj_name if has_name else ""

                fields_dict = cast(dict[str, Any], fields)

                # Real EnergyPlus epJSON is canonical for extensible types, but
                # hand-authored or legacy epJSON sometimes uses flat suffixed
                # keys (vertex_x_coordinate_2, time_3, ...). Coerce them into
                # the canonical wrapper-array shape so downstream consumers see
                # uniform storage.
                if pc and pc.extensible and pc.ext_wrapper_key and pc.ext_field_names:
                    fields_dict = drop_blank_group_slots(_bucket_flat_extensibles(fields_dict, pc), pc.ext_wrapper_key)

                field_order = list(base_field_names) if base_field_names is not None else None
                # A copy, without blank values ("" or null): a blank field is unset, as in IDF (idfkit#183).
                obj_data = {key: value for key, value in fields_dict.items() if not is_blank_slot(value)}
                if normalize_choices and pc is not None:
                    canonicalize_choices(obj_data, pc)
                if has_name and pc is not None and "name" in obj_data:
                    self._drop_body_name(obj_type, obj_name, obj_data)
                unknown_fields.extend(
                    self._unknown_fields(obj_type, obj_name, obj_data, pc, strict_parsing=strict_parsing)
                )

                obj = IDFObject(
                    obj_type=obj_type,
                    name=name,
                    data=obj_data,
                    schema=obj_schema,
                    field_order=field_order,
                    ref_fields=ref_fields,
                    extensibles=frozenset(pc.ext_field_names) if pc else None,
                    wrapper_key=pc.ext_wrapper_key if pc else None,
                    ext_inner_names=tuple(pc.ext_inner_props.keys()) if pc else (),
                    aliases=pc.field_aliases if pc else None,
                )

                addidfobject(obj)

        _raise_unknown_fields(unknown_fields)

    def _drop_body_name(self, obj_type: str, obj_name: str, obj_data: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        """Drop a ``name`` key repeated inside a named object's body.

        The object's key is its name; some writers repeat it in the body as well. EnergyPlus reads
        the key, so a body name that differs from it is logged and dropped too.
        """
        body_name = obj_data.pop("name")
        if not isinstance(body_name, str) or body_name.upper() != obj_name.upper():
            logger.warning(
                "%s '%s' in %s repeats a different name, %r, in its body; the key is the name",
                obj_type,
                obj_name,
                self._filepath,
                body_name,
            )

    def _unknown_fields(
        self, obj_type: str, obj_name: str, obj_data: dict[str, Any], pc: ParsingCache | None, *, strict_parsing: bool
    ) -> list[ParseDiagnostic]:
        """The keys of *obj_data* that no release ever had as fields of *obj_type*, one diagnostic each.

        EnergyPlus ignores a key that is not a field, so a misspelt field's value is silently
        lost and the field takes its default. With *strict_parsing* those are returned, to be
        raised; without, each is logged and kept, as before. A field an earlier release had, and
        this one removed, is logged and kept either way: EnergyPlus's own example files carry
        some, and EnergyPlus runs them.
        """
        if pc is None:
            return []
        unknown = [key for key in obj_data if key not in pc.known_keys]
        if not unknown:
            return []
        candidates = (*pc.known_keys, *pc.ext_field_names)
        diagnostics: list[ParseDiagnostic] = []
        for key in unknown:
            if key in get_schema_manager().field_names_in_any_release(obj_type):
                logger.warning(
                    "Field '%s' of %s '%s' in %s is not in this release's schema; EnergyPlus ignores it",
                    key,
                    obj_type,
                    obj_name,
                    self._filepath,
                )
                continue
            message = f"Unknown field '{key}' for {obj_type}"
            suggestion = closest_name(key, candidates)
            if suggestion is not None:
                message += f". Did you mean '{suggestion}'?"
            if not strict_parsing:
                logger.warning("%s in %s [name: %s]; kept as is", message, self._filepath, obj_name)
                continue
            diagnostics.append(
                ParseDiagnostic(
                    message=message,
                    filepath=str(self._filepath),
                    obj_type=obj_type,
                    obj_name=obj_name,
                    code="InvalidField",
                )
            )
        return diagnostics

    def _unknown_type(
        self, obj_type: str, objects: dict[str, Any], schema: EpJSONSchema, *, strict_parsing: bool
    ) -> None:
        """Raise for an object type *schema* does not have, or, without *strict_parsing*, log it."""
        suggestion = closest_name(obj_type, schema.object_types)
        message = f"Unknown object type '{obj_type}'"
        if suggestion is not None:
            message += f". Did you mean '{suggestion}'?"
        if not strict_parsing:
            logger.warning("%s in %s; skipped %d object(s)", message, self._filepath, len(objects))
            return
        diagnostic = ParseDiagnostic(
            message=message,
            filepath=str(self._filepath),
            obj_type=obj_type,
            obj_name=next(iter(objects), None),
            code="UnknownObjectType",
        )
        summary = "Failed to parse epJSON"
        raise IDFParseError(summary, diagnostics=[diagnostic])

    def get_epjson_version(filepath: Path | str) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
    """
    Quick version detection from epJSON file.

    Args:
        filepath: Path to epJSON file

    Returns:
        Version tuple (major, minor, patch)

    Raises:
        VersionNotFoundError: If version cannot be detected

    Examples:
        Detect the EnergyPlus version of an epJSON file:

            ```python
            from idfkit.epjson_parser import get_epjson_version

            version = get_epjson_version("SmallOffice.epJSON")
            print(f"EnergyPlus v{version[0]}.{version[1]}")
            ```
    """
    filepath = Path(filepath)

    with open(filepath, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        # Parse just enough to get version
        data = json.load(f, parse_constant=_constant_refuser(filepath))

    version_obj = data.get("Version")
    if version_obj:
        for _name, fields in version_obj.items():
            version_str: str = fields.get("version_identifier", "")
            if version_str:
                parts = version_str.split(".")
                major = int(parts[0]) if len(parts) > 0 else 0
                minor = int(parts[1]) if len(parts) > 1 else 0
                patch = int(parts[2]) if len(parts) > 2 else 0
                return (major, minor, patch)

    raise VersionNotFoundError(str(filepath))
